title.narrative: Skills and lifelong learning to facilitate access to and transitions in the labour market.

description.narrative:
Developing skills and promoting lifelong learning are essential to achieving full and productive employment, fostering sustainable enterprises and decent work for all in Asia and the Pacific. In labour markets shaped by digital transformation, demographic change, climate transition and globalisation, workers and enterprises must continuously adapt to remain competitive and resilient.
The ILO supports governments and social partners to strengthen inclusive, future-ready skills and TVET systems that improve school-to-work transitions, promote upskilling and reskilling, and bridge the digital divide — with particular attention to youth, women, migrant workers and those in vulnerable situations.
At the regional level, the ILO’s work on skills/TVET is well-aligned to support the implementation of the ASEAN HRD Roadmap and the workplans of ALMM, SLOM and the ASEAN TVET Council. This work and collaboration are anchored through the ILO-ASEAN Work Programme 2021-2025 as well as the Work Programme for 2026-2030 which is currently being approved for adoption. The ILO contributes to ASEAN cooperation on lifelong learning, labour market and skills intelligence, skills for digital and green transformation, skills recognition and mobility as well as workplace learning including apprenticeships. ILO supports ASEAN policy initiatives including the formulation of ASEAN Declarations and workplans related to skills and TVET and capacity building of our partners in ASEAN Member States while strengthening partnerships with workers’ and employers’ organisations and expanding knowledge on good practices. Together, these efforts enhance employability, productivity and sustainable growth, advancing social justice across the region.
